claim: The base model architecture and model scale influence the safety level of post-trained LLMs: LLaMA-based models are safer than Qwen-based models, and larger models are safer than smaller ones.
falsifier: Compare safety refusal rates across post-trained LLMs with different base architectures (e.g., LLaMA, Qwen) and different parameter counts, controlling for post-training data and procedure.

conditions: Models are post-trained for reasoning capabilities
Safety is evaluated on harmful prompts using the same benchmark
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the compared models (R1-7B Qwen-based, R1-8B LLaMA-based, R1-14B larger) and the specific post-training procedure; transfer to other base architectures or scales is unestablished.

title: Base model architecture–Safety behavior principle
